Symmetric-matrix eigenvalue expansion gives the claimed Rician and fixed-squeeze normal limits. value.rationale: Principal curvature anisotropy is a natural intrinsic geometric mark of time-frequency local concentration. The exact curvature-ratio law has the nontrivial \(r^{-2}\) heavy tail and infinite variance; the Rician crossover identifies a sharp competition between stochastic peak-shape fluctuations and Gaussian-window dilation of order \(h^{-1/2}\), with a distinct Gaussian fixed-squeeze regime. These are motivated structural statistics beyond previously known peak counts and heights, with a plausible use in quantifying shape of noise-dominated spectrogram peaks.
